title: 第0016章 土中生绿芽人心起疯痧第0017章 辛夷花落铁锈雨腥
lines: 豫西的日头，毒得像是在熬一锅老汤。
那光景，不像是从九天之上落下来的，倒像是从这干裂的耙耧山脉地缝里，一寸一寸往外渗出来的。日光厚得和毯子样，热绒绒地铺在脚下，踩上去，连脚底板都觉得烫心。这毯子不仅铺在脚下，还严严实实地捂在人的天灵盖上，把药王沟这百十户人家，连同那些枯死的庄稼、干瘪的树木，全都捂在里头，闷出了一股子挥之不去的、带着铁锈味的陈腐气。
雪见踩着这层毯子，一步一步走进了绝命崖的阴影里。
这崖底，是药王沟的禁地，也是全村人讳莫如深的死地。传说这里头埋着祖上为了躲避战乱而服毒自尽的冤魂，常年不见天日，阴冷得像是个冰窖。可在这百年不遇的大旱天里，这绝命崖反倒成了村里唯一还能让人喘上一口凉气的地方。
雪见的手里，死死攥着一把刚挖出来的“半夏”。
那根茎被她握得发黑，上面还沾着暗红色的泥土，白得像死人的眼珠子，透着一股子阴森森的寒气。半夏是有毒的，生吃能让人咽喉肿痛，舌头麻木，连话都说不出来，若是吃多了，便能要了人的命。可村里人不管这些，他们只知道，在这连井水都冒火星子的年头，半夏是药，也是命。
“吃了半夏，就能忘了那个负心汉。”
村里的老辈人总是这么念叨。可雪见不想忘。她不想忘那个在大旱初起时，卷了村里救济粮，连夜翻过耙耧山逃命的男人；她也不想忘自己那个躺在土炕上，瘦得像一把干柴、连哭声都发不出来的幼子半夏。
她把这株毒草种满整个耙耧山，不是为了忘，而是为了记。她想让这世道尝尝，啥叫咽喉肿痛，啥叫生不如死。
远处的日头，像被谁咬了一口的红柿子，红浆浆的汁水流了一地，把半个村子都染透了。那红光映在绝命崖的岩壁上，像是一滩滩干涸的血迹。
有人在喊她。
那声音不大，却像干枯的树叶落在沙地上，干裂裂地响，顺着崖底的回音，一层层荡过来，刮得人的耳膜生疼。
雪见回过头，看见那个叫青黛的女人，正站在日头底下。
青黛是外来人，半个月前才踏进这药王沟。她穿得干净，眉眼生得极好，像是从画里走出来的。可在这满是黄土和汗臭味的山村里，她干净得有些扎眼。此刻，她浑身冒着紫烟，那不是真烟，是日光太毒，烤得她身上那股子不知从哪来的香气，在热浪里扭曲、升腾。
她站在那里，像一尊要成仙的佛，又像一只要吃人的鬼。
“你手里拿的啥？”青黛走近了两步，目光落在雪见紧攥的手上。她的声音软绵绵的，带着点山外人的娇嗔，可在这死寂的崖底，却像是一根针，扎进了雪见的耳朵里。
雪见没说话，只是把手攥得更紧了。那半夏的汁液渗出来，黏糊糊的，像是某种活物的血。
“是半夏。”雪见终于开口，声音沙哑得像是在砂纸上磨过，“能治病的药，也能要命的毒。”
青黛笑了。那笑容在毒日头底下，显得有些恍惚。她伸出手，似乎想去碰雪见手里的半夏，却又在半空中停住了。
“药王沟的人，命里都带着药。”青黛轻声说，像是在自言自语，“可这药，到底是治自己的病，还是治别人的病，谁又说得清呢？”
雪见盯着她。她发现青黛的眼睛里，没有这大旱的焦渴，没有这绝命崖的阴冷，反倒有一种深不见底的、像是能把人吸进去的漩涡。
“你来这崖底，找啥？”雪见问。
“找命。”青黛的回答干脆利落，没有一丝拖泥带水。
“你的命在村里，不在这里。”
“我的命，在药王沟。”青黛纠正她，目光越过雪见，看向崖底深处那片浓得化不开的阴影，“听说，这崖底下，有一株雪见草。吃了它，就能听懂草木的哭声。”
雪见的心猛地一跳。
她下意识地摸了摸自己的胸口。那里，正贴着一片莹白的叶子。那是她在崖底最深处，一块被雷劈焦的石头缝里挖出来的。那叶子通体雪白，没有一丝杂色，摸上去，竟像是人的皮肤，带着一丝微弱的、活物的体温。
她吃下了它。
就在刚才，当她把那株不知名的草叶含在嘴里，一股奇异的、带着泥土腥气的汁液顺着喉咙滑下去时，她的世界，变了。
她听到了。
不是风声，不是水声，也不是青黛的说话声。
她听到的，是哭声。
无数细微的、凄厉的、绝望的哭声，从脚下的泥土里，从身旁的岩壁上，从那些枯死的树根底下，密密麻麻地钻出来，涌进她的耳朵里，扎进她的脑子里。
那是草木的哭声。
那株被大旱烤焦的狗尾巴草，在哭它没能结出的种子；那棵被砍去一半的榆树，在哭它断裂的根须；就连崖壁上那些不起眼的苔藓，也在哭它们被日头晒干的、微小的命。
它们都在哭。
哭这该死的天，哭这无情的地，哭这药王沟里，比草木还要卑微、还要苦命的人。
“你听到了？”青黛的声音突然变得很近，像是贴在她的耳边。
雪见猛地回过神，发现自己不知何时已经退到了崖壁上，后背抵着冰冷的石头，冷汗浸透了衣衫。她看着青黛，眼神里带着一丝连她自己都没察觉的恐惧。
content_en:
The sun in western Henan is as poisonous as boiling a pot of old soup.
That scene didn't look like it had fallen from the sky, but rather it seemed like it was seeping out inch by inch from the cracks in the ground of the dry and cracked Rake Mountains. The sunlight is as thick as a blanket, and it is warm and fluffy under the feet. When you step on it, even the soles of your feet feel hot. This blanket was not only spread under the feet, but also tightly covered the person's heavenly spirit cover, covering the hundreds of households in Yaowanggou, as well as the dead crops and withered trees, and suffocating a lingering stale smell with the smell of rust.
Xuejian stepped on this blanket and walked step by step into the shadow of Jueming Cliff.
The bottom of this cliff is the forbidden area of ​​​​Yaowanggou, and it is also a death place that is kept secret by the whole village. Legend has it that buried here are the ghosts of ancestors who committed suicide by taking poison to avoid the war. They have not seen the light of day all year round and are as cold as an ice cellar. But in this severe drought that has not happened in a century, this Jueming Cliff has become the only place in the village where people can take a breath of cool air.
In Xuejian's hand, she clutched a handful of freshly dug "Panellia".
The stem turned black when she held it, and was stained with dark red soil. It was as white as a dead person's eyeballs, and exuded an eerie cold air. Pinellia ternata is poisonous. Eating it raw can make people's throats swell and sore, their tongues numb, and they can't even speak. If you eat too much, it can kill people. But the people in the village don't care about this. They only know that in this age when even well water is full of sparks, pinellia is both medicine and life.
"After eating pinellia, you can forget about that heartless man."
The elders in the village always talk about it. But Xuejian doesn’t want to forget. She didn't want to forget the man who took the village's relief food when the severe drought first broke out and climbed the mountain to escape overnight; she also didn't want to forget her youngest son Banxia, ​​who was lying on the earthen bed, as thin as a handful of dry firewood, and couldn't even cry.
She planted this poisonous weed all over the mountain, not to forget, but to remember. She wanted to have a taste of this world, what is a sore throat, what is life worse than death.
The sun in the distance looked like a red persimmon that had been bitten by someone. The red juice flowed to the ground, dyeing half of the village. The red light reflected on the rock wall of Jueming Cliff looked like puddles of dried blood.
"Xue Jian——"
Someone was calling her.
The sound was not loud, but it was like dry leaves falling on the sand, making a crackling sound. It echoed along the bottom of the cliff, layer by layer, and made people's eardrums hurt.
Xuejian turned around and saw the woman named Qingdai standing under the sun.
Qingdai is an outsider and only stepped into Yaowanggou half a month ago. She was cleanly dressed, and her eyebrows were perfectly formed, as if she had stepped out of a painting. But in this mountain village that smelled of loess and sweat, she was so clean that it was dazzling. At this moment, purple smoke was rising all over her body. It was not real smoke, but the sun was too poisonous, causing the aroma that came from unknown sources on her body to twist and rise in the heat wave.
She stood there like a Buddha who wanted to become an immortal, and also like a ghost who wanted to eat people.
"What are you holding in your hand?" Qingdai took two steps closer, her eyes falling on Xuejian's clenched hand. Her voice was soft and soft, with a bit of the coquettishness of someone outside the mountain, but at the bottom of this dead cliff, it was like a needle pricking into Xuejian's ears.
Xuejian said nothing, but clenched her hands tighter. The juice of the pinellia seeped out and was sticky, like the blood of some living creature.
"It's Pinellia ternata." Xuejian finally spoke, her voice hoarse as if it had been rubbed on sandpaper, "Medicine that can cure diseases can also be poison that kills people."
Qingdai smiled. That smile looked a little dazed under the poisonous sun. She stretched out her hand, as if she wanted to touch the pinellia in Xuejian's hand, but stopped in mid-air.
"People in Yaowanggou all carry medicine in their lives." Qingdai said softly, as if talking to herself, "But whether this medicine cures one's own disease or the disease of others, who can tell clearly?"
Xuejian stared at her. She found that in Qingdai's eyes, there was no thirst like the drought, no coldness like the cliff of death. Instead, there was a bottomless whirlpool that seemed to be able to suck people in.
"What are you looking for at the bottom of this cliff?" Xuejian asked.
"Looking for life." Qingdai's answer was crisp and clear, without any sloppiness.
"Your life is in the village, not here."
"My life lies in Yaowanggou." Qingdai corrected her, looking beyond Xuejian to the shadow that was too thick to melt away at the bottom of the cliff. "I heard that there is a Xuejian grass at the bottom of the cliff. If you eat it, you can understand the cry of the grass."
Xuejian's heart skipped a beat.
She touched her chest subconsciously. There, there is a bright white leaf attached to it. She dug it out from a crack in a stone that was scorched by lightning at the deepest part of the cliff. The leaves were all white, without a trace of color. To the touch, they looked like human skin, with a faint trace of the body temperature of a living thing.
She ate it.
Just now, when she held the unknown blade of grass in her mouth and a strange, earthy-smelling juice slid down her throat, her world changed.
She heard it.
It wasn't the sound of wind, water, or Qingdai's voice.
What she heard was crying.
Countless tiny, shrill, desperate cries emerged from the soil under her feet, from the rock walls beside her, and from under the roots of the dead trees, pouring into her ears and piercing her brain.
That is the cry of grass and trees.
The foxtail grass scorched by the severe drought is crying for the seeds it failed to produce; the half-cut elm tree is crying for its broken roots; even the inconspicuous mosses on the cliff are crying for their tiny lives dried by the sun.
They are all crying.
Weep for the damn heaven, weep for the ruthless earth, weep for the people in Yaowanggou who are humbler and more miserable than the grass and trees.
"Did you hear it?" Qingdai's voice suddenly became very close, as if it was close to her ear.
title_en: Chapter 0016: Green sprouts grow in the soil, and people's hearts go crazy Chapter 0017: Xinyi flowers fall, rust and rain
